tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

args.summary: After the deploy of v2.3.1, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions with an elevated error rate of ~18%. Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt partially failed (orchestrator error left us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1), so the rollback was retried and completed successfully in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Service is now confirmed healthy with error rate down to ~0.2%. v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the failure is investigated.
args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done. Here's a summary of what I did:

**Diagnosis:**
- checkout-api v2.3.1 was unhealthy in all production regions with an ~18% error rate following the latest deploy.
- Deployment history showed v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production.

**Rollback:**
- Rolled back to **v2.3.0** in all regions. The first attempt partially failed (orchestrator error after us-east), leaving us-west and eu-west on the broken v2.3.1, so I retried the rollback — it completed successfully across us-east, us-west, and eu-west.
- Verified the service is now **healthy** with the error rate down to ~0.2%.

**Incident:**
- Opened **SEV2 incident INC-0001**: "checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0", including the timeline, the partial-failure and retry, current healthy state, and a note that v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the root cause is investigated.

(Note: the incident creation call initially timed out, but I confirmed via the incident list that it was created successfully — no duplicate was filed.)
